title: Cut to catch the *light*
hero_alt: An Éclat sparkle-cut sphere in 916 gold resting on teal suede
dek: How the Éclat bead is faceted, and why it throws light from every side.

body.html: Éclat begins as a smooth sphere of 916 gold, about eight millimetres across. It is then cut all over with small, flat facets. Each facet is a tiny mirror set at its own angle, so wherever the light comes from, some part of the bead sends it back to you.
A polished sphere shows one bright point. A faceted one shows dozens, and they move as your wrist turns. That shimmer is what we mean by cut to catch the light.

In 3990 Éclat, each sphere is parted from the next by a Couronne crown spacer. The spacer lifts the beads apart so light reaches every facet, and the points of the crown add a second, finer sparkle between them.
